title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous and next pages. X is a smooth complex curve with ω = Ω¹_X. A projective connection c_0 is fixed; in modern terms this is a projective structure, i.e. an sl2-oper. Grothendieck encodes it as a principal bundle 𝒯 (for PGL2 or a related group) with a Borel reduction, given by a section σ of the P¹-bundle P = 𝒯/B, and a flat connection. To a connection D on ω one attaches a projective connection c_D. For a local coordinate t, D_t is the trivial connection with D_t(dt)=0. Changing to another coordinate s gives D_s = D_t − ds'/s', where s' = ds/dt.

This page. The problem is to solve D_s = D for a given connection D = D_t + ϖ, with ϖ = λ(t)dt. The equation −ds'/s' = ϖ becomes s''/s' = −λ, i.e. (log s')' = −λ. So log s' = −Λ + const, where Λ is a primitive of λ. Then s' = c·exp(−Λ) with c ≠ 0, and s = c∫exp(−Λ)dt + c'. Hence solutions exist locally, in fact on any simply connected domain. They form an analytic torsor under the affine group Aff¹ = Aut(E¹) acting by s ↦ as+b. Within the PGL2-torsor of horizontal developing maps, this is the sub-torsor under the Borel B of maps whose induced section lies over the given section σ.

Quotienting by the unipotent radical B_u ≅ G_a (translations) forgets the additive constant. What remains is the 1-form φ = ds = s'dt, characterised as a nowhere-vanishing φ ∈ Γ(ω) with D_ξ = D (where φ = dξ), equivalently Dφ = 0.

The page then sets out a dictionary of horizontal analytic sections along the tower 𝒯 → 𝒯/B_u → 𝒯/B = P, restricted to sections σ' disjoint from σ:
(1) Horizontal sections of P are connections D on ω with c_D = c_0. On the next page this becomes the Riccati equation 2λ' + λ² = μ.
(2) Horizontal sections of 𝒯/B_u are pairs (D, φ) with c_D = c_0, φ a section of ω, and Dφ = 0. This is a linear first-order equation.
(3) Horizontal sections of 𝒯 are étale maps s : X^an → E¹(C) with s*(c) = c_0, i.e. c_{D_s} = c_0. This is the Schwarzian equation −2s'''/s' + 3(s''/s')² = μ.
The canonical maps between these levels are t ↦ (D_t, dt) ↦ D_t.

The marginal notes ('algébrique?' versus 'analytique–transcendante') mark which levels are algebraic and which are transcendental. This is the classical linearisation of the Schwarzian/Riccati equations, recast as reductions of a flat PGL2-bundle with Borel reduction. It serves the description of the uniformisation / developing-map sheaf U ⊂ Apphol(X^an, P¹(C)) as a torsor.
errors: On the line 's' = c^te exp Λ(t)' the minus sign is dropped; it should read exp(−Λ(t)). It is restored in the next formula s = c^te ∫ exp −Λ(t) dt + c^te. This is a trivial slip.

'Solutions exist globally' holds only on simply connected open sets (or locally). Globally the affine torsor may be non-trivial, through the monodromy of exp(−Λ). Grothendieck implicitly treats this as a torsor statement, which is correct.

ideas.modern_name: Developing maps of an affine structure / first-order linear ODE

missed.claim: Grothendieck works out the algebro-geometric 'oper' formalism for projective structures: a flat P¹-bundle with a transverse section, and the hierarchy of its horizontal sections modulo B, B_u and the trivial group. He does this in the same dossier as the Cartier operator and Gauss–Manin material. The content is classical, but the framing anticipates the oper language later used by Beilinson–Drinfeld, and in characteristic p by Mochizuki (dormant opers and p-curvature). The page itself does not carry out any characteristic-p step.
missed.quote: Sections analytiques de 𝒯/B_u horizontales ... couples (D,φ) ... telle que c_D = c_0, φ ∈ Γ(ω) telle que Dφ = 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents an early Grothendieck treatment of projective structures as reductions of flat PGL2-torsors, possibly linked in the dossier to Cartier operators and p-curvature. That combination is later central to p-adic Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the classical Riccati/linear/Schwarzian dictionary for projective structures. Its torsor/oper-style framing is natural for Grothendieck and only mildly anticipates later language. Nothing on this page is a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 is largely illegible; it ends with '⇒ ϖ = λ(t)dt'. The form is ϖ (varpi) as on the previous page, not ω.
'(log s')' = −λ(t)': the transcription's 'log s'' should read log s' throughout.
's' = c^te exp Λ(t)' with '≠0' under the constant. The image appears to lack the minus sign on this line.
'Aut_C(E¹(C)) = (Aut E¹_C)^an' rather than 'Aut C(E'(C))'. Here E¹ is the affine line.
'Sections σ' de P (= 𝒯/B) horizontales disjointes de σ' and 'disjointes' rather than 'dispensées'.
The marginal notes read approximately 'algébriques?' and 'analytique–transcendantes'.
'morphismes s : X^an → E¹_C telles que s*(c) = c_0' rather than 's : E × 𝒯 → E'_C'.
